title: One In, One Out
idea: A function takes each input to exactly one output, and f(3) means the output when the input is 3.
misconceptions: Treats f(x) as f × x, so a factor inside the bracket comes out
Squares the minus sign too: −x² is −(x²), not (−x)²
Answers with the output when the input is asked for (e.g. a height when a time is asked)
Interprets P(0) as 'zero population' instead of the initial value
Squares without brackets, so the sign comes out wrong
Works left to right, ignoring the order of operations

estimate.basis: Worked out by tools/explainer-scripts.mjs (runs, recordedWords). Recorded words count every line in the file, every branch included, and leave out callbacks.json and reactions.json, which are recorded once for every lesson. The main path takes the longest branch at each action, and the time is 150 spoken words a minute plus the pause and the cue. Player actions are player-paced and not counted.

notes: Format 3 (FAL-1087, #216): the Writer's edited proposal (writing/explainers/proposals/one-in-one-out.interactive.md, FAL-1086) as JSON, in the four acts. The id is unchanged, so the watched record and the manifest still point here.

Line ids: a line whose say is word for word the approved script's keeps its id: the two turns (10 lines), the slip's tap-line right and not-yet lines, the slip joke, the recap's first line and "Next time we run the relay backwards". Every other line is new, and the approved script's lines are retired in the manifest.

The recap's last line in the proposal, "Next time we run the relay backwards. Output in, input out. That's the transmission. Rook, out.", is two lines here, so the first keeps its recorded-once id (d1ax0c).

No recall section, as in the proposal: the Writer left that to the format (#216). builds_on still names ex.foundations.pre-substitute. The opener's call and the send of −3 teach the bracket, and the "any other call" line says (−3)² is +9, so a player who hasn't watched Tess can carry on. Adding Rook's tin-can-tess callback lines back is a Writer decision.

The build is two steps, not the proposal's three. The third step's wrong tiles (= 9, = −1 after = 5 − 4) had no misconception in the map for −1, and a wrong tile is keyed to one (#216). Rook's closing line now writes = 1 as he says "One.". The not-yet line "Five, take away four. Come in again." went with the step.

Misconception keys: the call's −13 is fn-pre-substitute#0 (squares without brackets: −3² − 4 = −13). Build tiles: 5 − −2² is fn-pre-substitute#0, (5 − −2)² is fn-pre-substitute#3 (works left to right), 5 + 4 is SL2.2.evaluate-notation#1 (the minus of −x² lost), 5 − (−4) is fn-pre-substitute#0.

Oupa's radio is the relay's broken variant, optional, with a second rule x² + 4, so every input gives two outputs (in 2 → out 0 and 8). The proposal gives no numbers for it. It plays after the oupa line and adds no words.
The first worked example is set at the east mast (problem.setting). The exam example keeps exam wording.

Every number was worked by the checker or by hand: (−3)² − 4 = 5, −3² − 4 = −13, x² − 4 = 12 at x = ±4 (both on the dial), g(−4) = 6 + 8 = 14, h(−2) = 5 − 4 = 1, C(0) = 20, C(5) = 80, 20 + 12t = 74 at t = 4.5 (inside 0 ≤ t ≤ 6), f(2) + f(3) = 8 + 11 = 19 against f(5) = 17.
The two turns are unchanged from the approved script, and still have their format 2 to-dos (not-yet lines to key to misconceptions). They are listed by --todo.
